sources.read: All six article pages; equation (12) and the plots inspected visually.
sources.finding: Photon-conserving model and energy decrease are prior work. Equations (1)-(16) do not explicitly state the arbitrary-field spectral energy identity, E-squared ceiling, or integrated retention bound.

sources.read: Energy and bright-soliton equations (12)-(23), with relevant supplemental energy integrals.
sources.finding: Equation (18) explicitly has E-squared divided by sech-width cubed in the long-pulse Raman approximation. The inverse-cube exponent and leading energy-loss coefficient are not a new physical effect.

sources.read: Sections II, III-C and appendices A-B; other material examples screened.
sources.finding: Positive measures and response sum rules are standard tools for passive-response bounds. Equations (50)-(59) give the general representation/sum-rule framework; the Raman energy-retention inequality was not found.

sources.read: Response/gain sections and limitations of the single oscillator; accessed complete PDF.
sources.finding: Multi-vibrational-mode response and gain model; the imaginary response is the Raman gain. Single-oscillator silica parameters are a common approximation with important fine-structure limitations. No energy-squared retention or arctangent intensity-norm bound found in the reviewed equations.
The single Lorentzian misses the silica Boson-peak shoulder; this supports restricting the exact sech formula to its explicitly specified oscillator response.

sources.read: Main theory and supplementary sections I.1-I.3, including the nonadiabatic convolution approximation.
sources.finding: Published preprint treats duration-dependent full-response SSFS in microresonators and nonadiabatic reduction. It uses a Raman-band approximation, not the exact trigamma energy-loss ratio, the energy-squared ceiling, or the arctangent concentration bound. Related short-pulse crossover physics is prior work.

sources.read: ZBLAN section 3 and table 1, including visual check of page 6.
sources.finding: Source of the fluoride oscillator, nonlinear index and mode-field diameter used here. The present beta2/beta3 values are declared surrogates, not extracted from its dispersion curve.
Foundational soliton self-frequency-shift width scaling; original full-text exact-overlap comparison remains unclosed.

Publisher abstract gives an inverse-duration short-pulse soliton frequency-shift regime. This is direct prior work on the short-pulse crossover; full-text comparison of the exact normalized ratio and its linear gap coefficient remains open.
sources.retrieval_note: Publisher PDF endpoint returned no accessible article text; ResearchGate article endpoint failed. No full-text access is claimed.

verdict: Leading long-pulse law is published; exact normalized curve, short-gap coefficient, and conditional arctangent bound were not found in this restricted search. Novelty is unestablished. The post-commit gpt-b comparison confirms the identity and weaker peak bound are already present internally; dynamical closure remains open. Herrmann and Nazarkin (1994) are additional direct short-pulse crossover prior work; only their publisher abstract was accessible.

internal_review_comparison.finding: Same exact spectral identity and weaker peak/supremum-weight ceiling. The new arctangent bound improves that conditional inequality but does not provide the missing propagated-concentration/peak closure.
